fatal_errors: The proposed Zr-doped aluminum system is unrelated to the target Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15 alloy.
It misses the relevant intervention: adjusting Fe/Co/Mn ratios and reducing phosphorus from 20 to 15 at.%.
It claims increased critical casting thickness without evidence; the target demonstrated amorphization only in approximately 20 micrometer melt-spun ribbons.
No supporting evidence or alloy-specific composition is provided.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses glass-forming ability and offers a falsifiable composition series, so it has broad problem alignment and a reasonably discriminating experimental design. However, it does not reconstruct the target material, compositional modification, phosphide/eutectic mechanism, baseline alloy, or measured thermal and structural outcomes. Its generic nucleation-suppression mechanism only weakly overlaps with the role of rapid quenching in the target. Because the proposed aluminum-Zr effect and critical-thickness improvement are unsupported by cited evidence or a defined base alloy, this is not a well-supported plausible alternative.
